newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bond yields sailed to their lowest levels in 16-months on Thursday as the wave of recent bullish economic announcement continued to sweep through the market.
At 1430 GMT, the R150 stock had berthed at 14.42 percent from 14.50 percent overnight after touching 14.395 percent earlier -- its lowest level since February 28 last year.

Dealers said the market initially began on a mixed note, as players tried to guage what outflows would stem from Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's announcement on Wednesday that local residents will be allowed to invest 200,000 rand offshore from July 1 when exchange controls are lifted.

The market then took its cue from comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals, who told state radio that he believed inflation had peaked and that short-term interest rates would continue to decline.

"I'm fairly optimistic the rate of inflation will continue to decline, that it will certainly stay below 10 percent for this year and by the end of the year it will be quite well below the present level of 9.5 percent."
Stals was commenting on Wednesday's release of May inflation data which came in below market forecasts of a 9.8 percent year-on-year rise.
He also said the central bank thought that the recent decline in short-end rates was part of a trend which should continue for the rest of the year.

His comments, which bolstered hopes for an interest rate cut in the second half of the year, enticed both foreign and local institutional buyers into the market -- hauling the R150 below its previous low of 14.46 percent by 0800 GMT.
The market, which has been bombarded with positive economic news of late, was not found wanting in the afternoon session either, when the Customs and Excise Department released May trade statistics.
The data showed a trade surplus of 1.75 billion rand -- more than double what analysts had hoped for.
But a lack of follow-through buying stemmed any further gains and the market consolidated between 14.44 and 14.40 percent for much of the afternoon session.
"The trade figure was very positive, but it only really helped confirm the trend," one trader said.
On Friday, dealers said they expected the R150 to test resistance at 14.38 percent, although some traders felt there was little to stop the market before it hit 14.10 percent.
On the currency market, the rand edged weaker as month-end importer dollar demand slightly outweighed exporter and offshore interest to sell.
In late trade, the rand was trading at 4.5100/5115 against the greenback from 4.5090/5010 overnight and after having trade in a 4.5000 to 4.5150 range all day.
"The rand traded in a relatively tight range given all the news on Stals and trade," a trader said. "There seems to be enough interest on both sides to keep it in this range for now."
Dealers said that some demand for dollars had come from banks looking to go long ahead of the expected demand for foreign currency on July 1.
At the top of the day's range, dealers said that the Reserve Bank was believed to be keen to show its hand around the 4.5150 to 4.5200 level.

Against the crosses, the rand was trading at 7.5128/5198 against sterling from 7.4979/5058, at 0.3831/3833 marks from 0.3822/3828 marks overnight and at 25.1890/2195 yen from 25.2462/2965 yen previously.

On the money market, three-month NCDs dipped to 15.85 percent offered from between 15.95 and 15.90 percent offered overnight, as the shortage dipped to 5.278 billion rand from 5.492 billion rand on Tuesday.
The BA rate stood at between 15.45 to 15.25 percent from 15.50 to 15.35 percent on Wednesday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 309.17 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 171.09 million rand's worth on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market on Wednesday were pegged at 10.33 billion rand from 6.64 billion rand before.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
